answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The violet multiplier is published, charged in lagoon, and relic lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3013 identities would post 1307 proofs and burn roughly 7 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
